plain.li: Ah. There it is.
Close the door, quick.
Give it a minute and you won't want to leave.
I can feel my toes again.
[snow] Snow on my boots, and in here it's summer.
[evening] Best part of the day, this.
[old] My knees are thanking me already.
[lowtech] Another ladle on the stones, if you can reach.
[child] It's so hot! Can I stay?

warm.li: Shift up, there's room for one more.
We should all come in here every day.

cheerful.li: I'm going to sit here until I melt!
Last one out has to fetch the water!

gloomy.li: Warm for an hour, then back out into it.
The cold's waiting outside the door, and it can wait.

cold.li: Twenty minutes, then back to work.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} sat in the heat of the sauna and talked about nothing much until they were both red in the face.
{PAWN_nameDef} kept pouring water on the hot stones, and {OTHER_nameDef} kept complaining about the steam.
{OTHER_nameDef} told {PAWN_nameDef} a few things in the sauna that {OTHER_pronoun} wouldn't have said anywhere else.
{PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} sat shoulder to shoulder in the sauna, too warm to argue about anything.
[snow] {PAWN_nameDef} dared {OTHER_nameDef} to roll in the snow after the sauna.
{PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} compared aches in the sauna and agreed that {OTHER_nameDef}'s back was the worse of the two.
{OTHER_nameDef} nearly nodded off in the sauna, and {PAWN_nameDef} let {OTHER_objective} be.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} warmed their hands and feet in the sauna and talked about the places they grew up.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} to stop talking and sweat.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} sang in the sauna until {OTHER_nameDef} joined in.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} sat in the sauna and agreed that the cold months were far too long.

plain.li: Not so deep, just a thumb's depth.
Keep the rows straight, the neighbors are watching.
Mind where you're stepping, that row's done.
Who's got the seed basket?
Smell that soil, it's ready.
[rain] Perfect weather for it, whatever your boots say.
[lowtech] A handful for the birds, so they leave the rest.
[child] I'm planting a whole row by myself!

warm.li: Good work, everyone, look how far we've got.
Take a breather, the ground isn't going anywhere.

cheerful.li: First one to the far end wins!
This is the best day of the year and nobody can tell me otherwise.

gloomy.li: All this, and one bad frost could take it.

cold.li: Keep the spacing even, it gives a better yield.

plain.li: May it come up thick and green.
Rain enough, sun enough, and no more frost.
That's the year started, then.
Whatever comes up here, it'll be ours.
[lowtech] To the ground, and back to us in the autumn.
[rain] Listen to the fields drinking.
Remember today when we're bringing it in.
Every row of it ours.

warm.li: Thank you, all of you, for a good day's work.
I'm glad we're all out here together.

cheerful.li: See you in the autumn, little ones!

gloomy.li: The rest is up to the weather now.

cold.li: The fields are in order, and the harvest should follow.

plain.li: Come on, you, home.
Easy, easy. This way.
One at a time through the gate.
That's it. Nearly there.
Who's got the last one?
[snow] Keep moving, you'll freeze standing there.
[afterraid] It's all right, they've gone, come on.
[evening] In before dark, that's the rule.
[child] It's following me, it likes me!

warm.li: There you go, warm straw tonight.

cheerful.li: Last one in gets the worst stall!

gloomy.li: It never wants to come in until it's too cold to stay out.

cold.li: Count them again at the door.

plain.li: [herd] Ropes, everyone, we're bringing the herd home.
[herd] Out to the grazing and back with every head of them.
[herd,snow] Ropes, and quick, before the snow gets deeper.

warm.li: [herd] Let's get them in somewhere warm, they've earned it.

plain.li: [herd] We walked the herd in on ropes, one by one. The stubborn one took three of us.
[herd] Brought the animals home with the others. My hands smell of rope and animal.

warm.li: [herd] Counting the animals in at the end was the best part of the day.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} has the seed sorted and the baskets by the door for {NAME}. Every pair of hands is wanted in the fields.
[first] It's the first {NAME}. {A_nameDef} wants it kept with the sowing, all hands together, and a word at the end.
[years] {YEARS} years of {NAME} now. The fields are waiting, and so is {A_nameDef}.
[tradition] The colony knows how {NAME} goes by now: the fields from morning, and a word at the edge in the evening.
[winter] The ground's still hard for {NAME}, but {A_nameDef} says they'll walk the fields together all the same and plan the rows.
[lowtech] For {NAME}, {A_nameDef} has set a handful of grain aside for the birds.

cheerful.li: It's {NAME}! {A_nameDef} has been up since before dawn and is already muddy to the knees.

gloomy.li: {A_nameDef} says a year that starts well on {NAME} has a better chance, and they could all use one.

plain.li: All of us in the fields today for {NAME}. My back aches just thinking about it.
[first] Our first {NAME}, with all of us out in the fields together. I hope it becomes a habit.
[years] Another {NAME}. Same fields, same seed baskets, a year older.
[tradition] Out to the fields together for {NAME}, as always. I've had my boots by the door since last night.

warm.li: Side by side in the dirt with the others for {NAME}. I like this day.

cheerful.li: It's {NAME}! I was up before anyone else.

gloomy.li: Whatever we do for {NAME}, the rest is up to the weather.

cold.li: Fieldwork for {NAME}. Sensible enough, if the ground allows.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about how far apart the rows should go.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} how {A_pronoun} was taught to sow as a child.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what {A_pronoun} hoped would come up this year.
[way:planting] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked over tomorrow's planting day and which fields to sow first.
